held.title: The version `sources` field is reused to store a version string, then parsed as a semver.
held.body: An unchanged refresh writes its own version string into the previous version's `sources` field (`sources=version`). Every later refresh then calls `semver.value(prev_ver.sources)` whenever that field is non-empty. `sources` is a general dataset-version metadata field. If an existing listing version has anything other than a semver string there, `semver.value` raises. That could be a listing made by an older release, one imported from Studio, or one with sources set some other way. The refresh would then fail on that `ValueError` and release its reservation, so `read_storage(update=True)` or an expired-TTL refresh breaks for that bucket. Writing into `sources` also overwrites whatever it held before. I could not see what older listings store in `sources`. The fix: keep the fence in a field reserved for it, or only parse `sources` when it is a valid version and treat anything else as no fence.
